lines.arrive: A shared pasture, with no rules yet. Anyone may graze their sheep here.
lines.herders: Four neighbours and you, two sheep each. With so few sheep, the grass grows back as fast as it's eaten.
lines.neighbour_adds: The blue house adds a sheep. It's their right.
lines.add_1: You let one more sheep out onto the common. A little more wool for you. The grass belongs to everyone.
lines.follow: Your neighbours notice. Two of them add sheep too.
lines.ask: Each extra sheep is all profit to its owner, and the cost is shared by everyone. So why would anyone stop?
lines.bell_hint: If nothing changes, it will all be eaten. You could ring the village bell, call the neighbours together, and agree on some limits.
lines.take_back: You bring one of yours back in to the pen. Nobody follows.
lines.bell: You ring the bell. The neighbours gather.
lines.agree_1: Together, you agree on limits: each household keeps the same number of sheep on the common, and the total is no more than the grass can feed.
lines.agree: So the extra sheep go home, yours along with everyone else's. Nobody owns the grass, but now you all look after it.
lines.tempt: Everyone is keeping to the limit. If just you let one more sheep out, it would be unfair, but the grass could take it, and the wool would be all yours. If everyone did, it couldn't. Will you let one more out?
lines.kept: You leave it in the pen. The limit holds.
lines.tempt_took: Just one. But your neighbours can count, and they can do the same sum.
lines.fray: One more each. Five extra sheep is more than the grass can feed, and it goes, for everyone.
lines.collapse: The grass is gone. For everyone.
lines.held_end: You held back. They didn't. The grass went anyway.
lines.took_back_end: You took yours back. It wasn't enough on your own.
lines.sheep: This one's yours: the teal mark. She has no idea about any of this.
lines.wool: Your wool. More sheep, more wool. For now.
